titel: The council's decrees: Haec sancta and the sentence
autor: The Council of Constance, sessions V (6 April 1415) and XV (6 July 1415)
quelle: Sacrorum conciliorum nova et amplissima collectio, ed. J. D. Mansi, vol. XXVII (Venice: Zatta, 1784), cols. 590 and 752–755. Internet Archive, sacrorumconcilio0027joan. Public domain.
hinweis: Mansi reprints the acts of Constance largely from Hermann von der Hardt's edition (1696–1700), whose fourth volume, with these sessions, is not available in a usable scan. The Latin was read against the page images; the long s, ligatures and accents are normalized. Excerpts; cuts are marked […]. The English is this site's working translation (CC0).

sections.blurb: After the pope's flight, the council declares that it has its power immediately from Christ, and that even a pope must obey it in matters of faith, union and reform.

units.titel: Haec sancta: the council above the pope
units.orig: Haec sancta Synodus Constantiensis generale Concilium faciens, pro exstirpatione ipsius schismatis, & unione & reformatione ecclesiae Dei in capite, & in membris, ad laudem omnipotentis Dei, in Spiritu sancto legitime congregata, ad consequendum facilius, securius, liberius unionem & reformationem ecclesiae Dei ordinat, diffinit, decernit, & declarat, ut sequitur. Et primo declarat, quod ipsa in Spiritu sancto legitime congregata, Concilium generale faciens, & ecclesiam catholicam repraesentans, potestatem a Christo immediate habet, cui quilibet cujuscumque status vel dignitatis, etiam si papalis exsistat, obedire tenetur in his quae pertinent ad fidem & exstirpationem dicti schismatis, & reformationem dictae ecclesiae in capite & in membris. Item, declarat, quod quicumque cujuscumque conditionis, status, dignitatis, etiam si papalis, qui mandatis, statutis seu ordinationibus, aut praeceptis hujus sacrae Synodi & cujuscumque alterius Concilii generalis legitime congregati, super praemissis, seu ad ea pertinentibus, factis, vel faciendis, obedire contumaciter contempserit, nisi resipuerit, condignae poenitentiae subjiciatur, & debite puniatur, etiam ad alia juris subsidia (si opus fuerit) recurrendo.
units.en: This holy synod of Constance, forming a general council, for the extirpation of the said schism and for the union and reform of the Church of God in head and members, to the praise of almighty God, lawfully gathered in the Holy Spirit, in order to achieve more easily, safely and freely the union and reform of the Church of God, ordains, defines, decrees and declares as follows. And first it declares that, lawfully gathered in the Holy Spirit, forming a general council and representing the catholic Church, it has its power immediately from Christ, and that everyone, of whatever state or dignity, even if it be papal, is bound to obey it in what concerns the faith, the extirpation of the said schism, and the reform of the said Church in head and members. Likewise it declares that anyone, of whatever condition, state or dignity, even papal, who contumaciously refuses to obey the mandates, statutes, ordinances or precepts of this holy synod, or of any other general council lawfully gathered, on the matters above or what concerns them, made or to be made, shall, unless he comes to his senses, be subjected to fitting penance and duly punished, recourse being had, if need be, to the other aids of the law.
units.note: Session V, Saturday 6 April 1415, two weeks after John XXIII's flight. The decree on which the council's authority rested: it deposed John XXIII in May and judged Hus in July under it. Mansi prints it from the first edition, with the words 'and the reform of the said Church in head and members' in the first article; some manuscripts lack them, and their place in the decree was argued over afterwards. The cut continues with orders that the pope may not move the curia from Constance.

sections.blurb: The definitive sentence read in the cathedral: Wyclif's disciple, a true and manifest heretic, whose appeal to Christ is a mockery of the Church's jurisdiction; degraded and left to the secular arm.

units.orig: Sacrosancta generalis Constantiensis Synodus, ecclesiam catholicam repraesentans, in Spiritu sancto legitime congregata, ad perpetuam rei memoriam. Quia teste Veritate, arbor mala fructus malos facere consuevit, hinc est, quod vir damnatae memoriae Joannes Wicleff sua mortifera doctrina non in Christo Jesu per evangelium, ut olim sancti patres filios genuere, sed contra Christi salutarem fidem velut radix virulenta plures genuit filios pestiferos, quos sui perversi dogmatis reliquit successores; adversus quos haec sancta Synodus tanquam contra spurios & illegitimos filios cogitur insurgere, & eorum errores ab agro Dominico tanquam vepres nocivas, cura pervigili & cultro auctoritatis ecclesiasticae resecare, ne ut cancer serpant in perniciem aliorum. [...] nihilominus tamen quidam Joannes Hus in hoc sacro Concilio hic personaliter constitutus, non Christi, sed potius Joannis Wicleff haeresiarchae discipulus, post & contra damnationem & decretum hujusmodi ausu temerario contraveniens, errores ejus plures & haereses, tam ab ecclesia Dei, quam etiam a certis olim reverendis in Christo patribus, dominis archiepiscopis & episcopis diversorum regnorum, & magistris in theologia plurium studiorum condemnatos, dogmatizavit, asseruit & praedicavit; praesertim damnationi scholasticae ipsorum articulorum Joannis Wicleff factae pluries in universitate Pragensi suis complicibus in scholis & in praedicationibus publice resistendo, ac ipsum Joannem Wicleff virum catholicum & doctorem evangelicum, in favorem ejus doctrinae, coram multitudine cleri & populi declaravit.
units.en: The most holy general synod of Constance, representing the catholic Church, lawfully gathered in the Holy Spirit, for a perpetual record. Since, as the Truth bears witness, a bad tree is wont to bear bad fruit, so it is that John Wyclif, a man of damned memory, by his deadly teaching, not in Christ Jesus through the gospel, as the holy fathers once begot sons, but against the saving faith of Christ, like a poisonous root begot many pestilent sons, whom he left as successors of his perverse doctrine; against whom this holy synod is compelled to rise as against bastard and illegitimate sons, and to cut away their errors from the Lord's field like harmful briars, with vigilant care and the knife of ecclesiastical authority, lest they creep like a cancer to the ruin of others. [...] Nevertheless a certain John Hus, here present in person at this holy council, a disciple not of Christ but rather of John Wyclif the heresiarch, after and against such condemnation and decree, contravening them with rash daring, taught, asserted and preached many of his errors and heresies, condemned both by the Church of God and by certain reverend fathers in Christ, lords archbishops and bishops of various kingdoms, and masters in theology of many universities; above all, with his accomplices, publicly resisting in the schools and in sermons the scholastic condemnation of those articles of John Wyclif made several times in the university of Prague, and, in favour of his teaching, declaring John Wyclif himself before a multitude of clergy and people to be a catholic man and an evangelical doctor.
units.note: Read in the cathedral on 6 July 1415 by Antonio, bishop of Concordia, after the council had condemned Wyclif's articles in the same session. The cut recalls the Roman council of 1412–13 that condemned Wyclif's books. The council's case begins with Wyclif and Prague, not with anything Hus said at Constance.

units.orig: Visis insuper actis & actitatis in causa inquisitionis de & super haeresi contra praedictum Joannem Hus habitis & factis, habita per prius fideli & plenaria commissariorum in hujusmodi causa deputatorum relatione, aliorumque magistrorum in theologia, ac doctorum juris utriusque in, de, & super actis, actitatis ac dictis testium fide dignorum & plurimorum, quae dicta ipsi Joannis Hus palam & publice lecta sunt coram patribus & praelatis hujus sacri Concilii, per quorum testium dicta apertissime constat, eumdem Joannem multa mala, scandalosa, seditiosa, & periculosas haereses dogmatizasse in publico, & per multa annorum curricula praedicasse: Christi nomine invocato haec sacrosancta Synodus Constantiensis, solum Deum prae oculis habens, per hanc diffinitivam sententiam, quam profert in his scriptis, pronunciat, decernit & declarat, dictum Joannem Hus fuisse & esse verum & manifestum haereticum, ipsumque errores & haereses ab ecclesia Dei dudum damnatas, & plurima scandalosa, piarum aurium offensiva, temeraria & seditiosa dogmatizasse, & publice praedicasse, in non modicam offensam divinae majestatis, ac universalis ecclesiae scandalum, & fidei catholicae detrimentum: claves etiam ecclesiae & censuras ecclesiasticas vilipendisse: in quibus per annos multos perstitit animo indurato, Christi fideles per suam pertinaciam nimium scandalizans, cum appellationem ad Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, tanquam ad summum judicem, omissis ecclesiasticis mediis interposuerit; in qua multa falsa & injuriosa posuit & scandalosa, ipsius sedis Apostolicae censurarum ecclesiasticarum & clavium in contemptum.
units.en: Having seen, moreover, the acts and proceedings had and done in the case of inquisition into heresy against the said John Hus, after a faithful and full report by the commissioners deputed in this case and by other masters in theology and doctors of both laws on the acts, proceedings and statements of very many trustworthy witnesses, which statements were read openly and publicly to the said John Hus before the fathers and prelates of this holy council, and by which it is most plainly established that the same John taught many evil, scandalous and seditious things and dangerous heresies in public and preached them for many years: calling on the name of Christ, this most holy synod of Constance, having God alone before its eyes, by this definitive sentence which it pronounces in these writings, pronounces, decrees and declares that the said John Hus was and is a true and manifest heretic, and that he taught and publicly preached errors and heresies long condemned by the Church of God, and very many things scandalous, offensive to pious ears, rash and seditious, to the no small offence of the divine majesty, the scandal of the universal Church and the detriment of the catholic faith; and that he despised the keys of the Church and ecclesiastical censures, persisting in this for many years with hardened mind, greatly scandalizing Christ's faithful by his pertinacity, when, setting aside the means of the Church, he lodged an appeal to our Lord Jesus Christ as to the supreme judge, in which he set down many false, injurious and scandalous things in contempt of the apostolic see, of ecclesiastical censures and of the keys.
units.note: The appeal to Christ (Hus's appeal of October 1412 from the pope to Christ, 'the most just judge') is named in the sentence itself as an offence. The sentence rests on the witnesses' depositions; Hus had answered that the articles drawn from them were false (Letters [4]).

units.titel: Degraded and left to the secular arm
units.orig: Idcirco propter praemissa & alia plura, praefatum Joannem Hus haereticum fuisse & esse haec sancta Synodus pronunciat, & tanquam haereticum judicandum & condemnandum fore judicat & condemnat per praesentes: dictamque appellationem tamquam injuriosam & scandalosam & illusoriam jurisdictionis ecclesiasticae reprobando, ipsumque Joannem Hus populum Christianum, maxime in regno Bohemiae, in praedicationibus suis publicis & scripturis per eum compilatis seduxisse, ac ejusdem populi Christiani non veracem praedicatorem evangelii Christi secundum expositionem sanctorum doctorum, sed fuisse verius seductorem. Verum quia per ea quae haec sacrosancta Synodus vidit & audivit, cognovit eumdem Joannem Hus pertinacem & incorrigibilem, & adeo totaliter, quod non cupiebat ad gremium sanctae matris ecclesiae redire, neque haereses & errores per eum publice defensatos & praedicatos velle abjurare. Idcirco hoc sacrum Concilium Constantiense eumdem Joannem Hus ab ordine sacerdotali, & aliis ordinibus, quibus exsistit insignitus, deponendum & degradandum fore declarat & decernit: [...] Haec sancta Synodus Constantiensis Joannem Hus, attento, quod ecclesia Dei non habeat ultra quid gerere valeat, judicio saeculari relinquere, ipsum curiae saeculari relinquendum fore decernit.
units.en: Therefore, for the above and much else, this holy synod pronounces that the said John Hus was and is a heretic, and judges and condemns him by these presents to be judged and condemned as a heretic; rejecting the said appeal as injurious, scandalous and a mockery of ecclesiastical jurisdiction; and declaring that the same John Hus seduced the Christian people, above all in the kingdom of Bohemia, in his public sermons and in the writings he composed, and was not a truthful preacher of the gospel of Christ to that Christian people according to the exposition of the holy doctors, but rather their seducer. And since, from what this most holy synod has seen and heard, it has recognized the same John Hus to be pertinacious and incorrigible, and so wholly so that he did not wish to return to the bosom of holy mother Church, nor to abjure the heresies and errors he had publicly defended and preached: therefore this holy Council of Constance declares and decrees that the same John Hus is to be deposed and degraded from the priestly order and the other orders with which he is marked [...]. This holy synod of Constance, considering that the Church of God has nothing further it can do, decrees that John Hus is to be left to the secular judgment, and relinquished to the secular court.
units.note: The cut names the archbishop of Milan and the bishops of Feltre, Asti, Alessandria, Bangor and Lavaur to carry out the degradation (Mlad. Sentence [2]). The council does not sentence to death; it 'relinquishes' the heretic, and the secular arm, here the king of the Romans, does the rest (Mlad. Sentence [3]).

sections.blurb: Five of the thirty articles condemned with Hus: the Church of the predestined, Peter not the head, the papacy from the emperor, the wicked pope a devil, and no lordship in mortal sin.

units.orig: Articuli damnati Joannis Hus, de quibus supra fit mentio. 1. Unica est sancta universalis ecclesia, quae est praedestinatorum universitas. Et infra sequitur: Universalis sancta ecclesia tantum est una, sicut tantum est numerus unus omnium praedestinatorum. [...] 7. Petrus non fuit, nec est caput ecclesiae sanctae catholicae. [...] 9. Papalis dignitas a Caesare inolevit, & Papae praefectio & institutio a Caesaris potentia emanavit. [...] 20. Si Papa est malus, & praesertim si est praescitus, tunc ut Judas Apostolus est diabolus, fur, & filius perditionis, & non est caput sanctae militantis ecclesiae, cum nec sit membrum ejus. [...] 30. Nullus est dominus civilis, nullus est praelatus, nullus est episcopus, dum est in peccato mortali.
units.en: The condemned articles of John Hus, of which mention is made above. 1. There is one holy universal Church, which is the whole number of the predestined. And it follows below: The universal holy Church is only one, as there is only one number of all the predestined. [...] 7. Peter was not, and is not, the head of the holy catholic Church. [...] 9. The papal dignity grew up from the emperor, and the appointment and institution of the pope came from the emperor's power. [...] 20. If the pope is wicked, and especially if he is foreknown to damnation, then like the apostle Judas he is a devil, a thief and a son of perdition, and is not the head of the holy Church militant, since he is not even a member of it. [...] 30. No one is a civil lord, no one is a prelate, no one is a bishop, while he is in mortal sin.
units.note: Thirty articles, most drawn from De ecclesia (1413). Hus did not deny that he had written many of them, but held that several were wrenched from their context; he had glossed them with his own hand in prison, and Mladoňovice records his answers in the cathedral. Article 30 frightened the princes as much as the prelates: a king in mortal sin would be no king. Article 20 was the charge against John XXIII made into heresy, a month after the council had deposed him.
